lesson.title: A fresh symmetry question
lesson.subtitle: P4 symmetry revision
lesson.objective: Count the lines of symmetry of a shape.
lesson.story: How many lines of symmetry does this rectangle have? If there are none, enter 0.

steps.title: Count the lines of symmetry
steps.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does this rectangle have? If there are none, enter 0.
hints: Think about folding the shape so that the two halves match exactly.
Try folding along the middle, along the corners, and in other directions.
Test each fold carefully. There are 2.
The rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry. Enter 2.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: Can a shape have no lines of symmetry?

choices.label: Yes, but only shapes with four sides can have no line of symmetry.
Yes. If no fold makes the halves match, it has no line of symmetry.
No. Every shape has at least one line of symmetry somewhere on it.

hints: Think about shapes that look tilted or uneven.
A fold must make the halves match exactly.
Some shapes cannot be folded to match.
Choose the explanation that says a shape can have none.
